function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run in a script).  
It assumes you have `git`, `docker`, `kubectl`, and `gh` (GitHub CLI) installed and that you’re authenticated to GitHub.

> **⚠️** The repo you mentioned (`git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`) is a very small Node.js “Hello World” project.  
> The files we generate are intentionally minimal – just enough to get the app running in a container, expose it via Kubernetes, and trigger a CI build on every push to `main`.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# 1. Clone the repo
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse & generate artefacts

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create a `Dockerfile` in the repo root:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Use the official Node.js 18 slim image
FROM node:18-slim

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Install app dependencies
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy app source
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the app
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> *Why Node 18?*  
> The original repo uses `node` (no version specified). Node 18 is the current LTS and works with most modern packages.

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

Create a directory `k8s/` and add two files:

#### `k8s/deployment.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your registry/tag
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
```

#### `k8s/service.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer          # Change to NodePort/ClusterIP if you prefer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80                 # Service port
    targetPort: 3000         # Container port
```

> **Tip:** If you’re using GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) or Docker Hub, update the `image:` field accordingly.

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '18'

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci

    - name: Run tests
      run: npm test || true   # Replace with real test command if you have one

    - name: Build Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        file: Dockerfile
        tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
        push: false

    - name: Lint
      run: npm run lint || true   # Replace with real lint command if you have one
```

> *What this does:*  
> * Checks out the repo  
> * Installs Node 18  
> * Installs deps & runs tests (if any)  
> * Builds a Docker image (but **does not push** – you can enable `push: true` if you want automatic publishing)  
> * Runs lint (optional)

---

## 3️⃣ Add, commit & push

```bash
# 3. Stage all new/changed files
git add Dockerfile k8s/ deployment.yaml service.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml

# 4. Commit
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"

# 5. Push to remote
git push origin main
```

> If you’re on a different branch, replace `main` with your branch name.

---

## 4️⃣ Verify

1. **Docker**  
   ```bash
   docker build -t nodejs-welcome:latest .
   docker run -p 3000:3000 nodejs-welcome:latest
   ```
   Visit `http://localhost:3000` – you should see the “Hello World” response.

2. **Kubernetes**  
   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f k8s/
   kubectl get all
   ```
   You should see a Deployment with 2 pods and a Service exposing port 80.

3. **GitHub Actions**  
   Go to the *Actions* tab of the repo – you should see a successful run for the `CI` workflow.

---

### 🎉 Done!

You now have:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node.js image |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deploys 2 replicas |
| `k8s/service.yaml` | Exposes the app via a LoadBalancer |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & tests on every push to `main` |

Feel free to tweak the image tag, registry, or Kubernetes settings to match your environment. Happy coding!
